title: Keep a risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies log
summary: A RAID log keeps track of risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies in one place, with owners and actions. It stops important problems slipping through.

beginner: Create one log with four sections: risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies.
For each item, write a short description, an owner and a next action.
Rate risks by how likely and how serious they are.
Review the log every week with the team.
Escalate the most serious items to your sponsor.
intermediate: Keep one RAID log with owners and actions.
experienced: Link RAID items to the plan and roadmap.
Use the log to drive decisions, not just record them.
Keep it short and focused on what matters.

canDelegateTo.task: Maintain the log and run reviews

toolExamples.confluence: Use a RAID log template on the project page.
toolExamples.jira: Track risks and dependencies as issues with owners.
toolExamples.sharepoint-word: Keep a shared log in a list with owners and dates.

definitionOfDone: Log created with owners and actions

sources.title: A product manager's guide to release planning (Atlassian)
